last_verdict: FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING — Frozen decision_rule triggers FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING on clause C3: no estimator passes BOTH C1 (|null_mean| < 0.1 bits) AND C3 (positive_control_k3 >= 0.5 bits, p <= 0.001). KSG CMI passes C1 (|null_mean|=0.012078 bits, 8.3x below threshold) but fails C3 (positive_control_k3=0.000560 < 0.5, 893x below threshold against true 1.52-bit CMI). LR passes C1 (|null_mean|=0.004515 bits, 22x below threshold) but fails C3 (positive_control_k3=0.103695 < 0.5, 4.8x below threshold). Audit REVISE corrects producer theoretical analysis: stochastic SPA produces I(Y;A|Z) ≈ 1.52 bits (not 0.004 as claimed), so C3 failure is genuine estimator insensitivity to a strong signal, not weak design. KSG null centering is achieved by near-zero output for all inputs (null_std=0.000187), not unbiased estimation of the true CMI. LR history collapse (K2=K3 exactly) persists on stochastic SPA, confirmed by degenerate control (deterministic SPA LR K3=0.104420 ≈ stochastic 0.103695).
next_question: Can an estimator with sufficient sensitivity — such as a plug-in transition-matrix KL divergence estimator (D_KL(P(Y|Z,A) || P(Y|Z)) computed directly on the stochastic SPA's empirical transitions), a KSG CMI variant with k=10 or k=20 to increase neighborhood resolution, or a permutation test conditioned on (state, action) strata — detect the demonstrated 1.52-bit CMI signal while preserving |shuffled-action null_mean| < 0.1 bits at N=5000, thereby resolving whether the insensitivity is specific to KSG k=5 and LR chi2-per-state, or fundamental to discrete CMI estimation on 12-state SPAs?
